messages:
Maya: Heads up - post-deploy, EU p95 token latency jumped ~18% vs baseline. Noticed ~10:02 UTC. :eyes:
Jonathan: saw that on dashboard, looks concentrated in eu-west-1, small error spike too (502s)
deploy-bot: [1723500020] Canary checks: p95_latency eu-west-1 = +18% > threshold(15%). Autopilot: no auto-rollback configured for this release because 'surgical_unwind' flag set.
Maya: we set surgical_unwind to avoid blunt rollback; plan was partial traffic shift then patch. Are we happy to manual-cutover?
Nora: I prefer targeted traffic-unwind to stable variant first. Can we move 20% traffic off new canary and monitor 10m?
Samir: Agree. Can do traffic shift now. Running command: ```rbctl traffic-shift --region eu-west-1 --from release/2024-03-xx --to release/stable --percent 20``` 
Samir: starting shift - will post when complete
Maya: also open a customer comm draft in /docs/release-notes/downtime.md? Need to flag if we roll fully.
Jonathan: If after 10m p95 doesn't improve, we should escalate to full rollback. Criteria: p95 > +10% and error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m.
deploy-bot: [1723500100] Traffic-shift job completed: 20% -> stable. New p95 delta: +12% (improved), errors down 0.3%
Nora: getting better. Keep observing 10m
Maya: I'll create a rollback ticket and prefill commands just in case. Ticket: RB-2024-331
Maya: prefilled rollback command: ```/deploy revert --version 2024-03-xx --regions eu-west-1,eu-central-1``` 
Samir: monitoring: p95 now +9% at 1723500200, errors 0.2%
Jonathan: suggest hold - no full rollback yet. But pin release on Dedicated pools? We should also pin dedicated GPU pools to stable model variant for any customer routing until we confirm.
Maya: yes, pin request sent to infra: ```infractl pin-variant --pool dedicated-eu --variant stable``` 
infra-bot: pinned dedicated-eu to stable at 1723500255 :white_check_mark:
Maya: going to update release notes: small perf regression in eu canary, mitigated by traffic split. Drafting comms to customers on Dedicated pool SLA implications.
Nora: Q - do we annotate the release notes with rollback decision path? I think yes: explain manual cutover criteria and expected timeline.
Jonathan: agreed. Also add runbook steps for engineers: include commands for partial and full rollback, and contact list.
Maya: final for now - continue monitor for 20m, we'll reconvene at +30.
Samir: :thumbsup: I'll keep watch on logs; will escalate immediately if error rate crosses 0.5% again.
deploy-bot: [1723500360] Canary check at +30: p95 delta +7%, errors 0.15% - marked STABLE. Closing active handoff.
Maya: great, followups: (1) update release notes, (2) close RB ticket as 'mitigated without full rollback', (3) retro postmortem tomorrow.
Jonathan: noted - will add timeline and operator actions in postmortem.
Nora: thanks everyone. :tada:
